# Mérida The cultural, academic, and economic metropolis of southeastern Mexico. Centered around a dense, historic colonial grid and rapidly expanding outward along concentric ring roads and radial avenues, Mérida challenges transit planners to unite sprawling suburban bedroom communities, booming financial and commercial corridors, a vast ecosystem of higher education campuses, and the northern coastal port of Progreso into a seamless, high-capacity regional network. ## Coverage Mérida and its metropolitan surroundings in Yucatán, including Kanasín, Umán, Progreso, Conkal and Ucú. Regional bounding box: -90.4507, 20.1571, -88.7191, 21.7741. Demand represents the retained map territory within this area. ## Population and Demand

## Map Features - Regional map tiles, roads and buildings index from the latest MID build. - Gulf/coastal bathymetry and runway/taxiway data. - Special-demand content metadata and Railyard sidecar files. - Starting view centered at latitude 20.94642, longitude -89.60565, zoom 10. ## Demographics and Methodology Demand V2 uses CPV 2020 urban-block employed-resident data and Marco 2020 geography for spatial distribution and placement. EIC 2025 municipal controls and weighted person microdata provide the 2025 population, employment and mobility reference. The modeled area is the retained map territory, rather than the full municipalities used for source controls. Destinations use physical DENUE establishment locations and establishment size-band priors. The effective workplace mode is historical_fine_transfer: municipal SCIAN/size groups use historical CE reference-year 2023 employment intensities where supported, and retain DENUE priors for missing, suppressed, excluded or unsupported groups. These are estimated attraction weights, not measured current jobs at each establishment. The report does not identify a DENUE reference year; no new DENUE vintage is claimed. Synthetic OD allocation uses municipal survey evidence as partial aggregate constraints, beta 0.12 as the requested reference (not a calibrated beta), connected permitted territories, and OSRM driving baselines. Final destination targets are normalized model weights, not observed workplace headcounts. University and airport demand is reserved within the traveler budget. Cohorts contain exactly 50 people, with an aggregate rounding increase of 519 travelers above the pre-cohort integer budget of 663,631, giving 664,150 exported travelers. CPV suppression is handled with aggregate residual/capacity reconstruction and limited fallback estimates described in the build report. CPV residential detail remains a 2020 spatial baseline; the 2025 controls and commuting observations are municipal, not new block-level observations. No claim of observed block-to-establishment OD, exact establishment employment, automatic tier improvement, or new game compatibility is made. ## Sources and Credits - Map author: Meszier83. - INEGI CPV 2020 and Marco Geoestadístico 2020: residential spatial distribution and placement. - INEGI EIC 2025: municipal controls and person-level mobility inputs. - INEGI DENUE and Censos Económicos, reference year 2023: establishment locations, size bands and historical employment intensity estimates. - © OpenStreetMap contributors and Geofabrik: cartography and road data. - OSRM: road driving baselines. - University enrollment and ASUR airport passenger inputs: configured special-demand attraction. ## Validation ZIP integrity, file provenance, demand references and special-demand relationships have been checked. In-game loading, save/reload and existing-save compatibility have not been verified for this exact build. ## License Open Database License (ODbL) for underlying OpenStreetMap data; the applicable INEGI open-data terms and licenses of the other source datasets apply.
